triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: After transcription, eukaryotic pre-mRNAs must undergo several processing steps before they can be translated.

triples.head: eukaryotic pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: Eukaryotic (and prokaryotic) tRNAs and rRNAs also undergo processing before they can function as components in the protein-synthesis machinery.

triples.head: eukaryotic pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The coding sequences (exons) are interrupted by noncoding introns, which must be removed to make a translatable mRNA.

triples.head: eukaryotic pre-mRNA

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The three most important steps of pre-mRNA processing are the addition of stabilizing and signaling factors at the 5' and 3' ends of the molecule, and the removal of the introns.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: In rare cases, the mRNA transcript can be 'edited' after it is transcribed.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The process of removing introns and reconnecting exons is called splicing.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: Some of the bases of pre-rRNAs are methylated; that is, a –CH3 methyl functional group is added for stability.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: As with pre-mRNAs, subunit excision occurs in eukaryotic pre-RNAs destined to become tRNAs or rRNAs.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The tRNAs and rRNAs are structural molecules that have roles in protein synthesis; however, these RNAs are not themselves translated. Pre-rRNAs are transcribed, processed, and assembled into ribosomes in the nucleolus. Pre-tRNAs are transcribed and processed in the nucleus and then released into the cytoplasm where they are linked to free amino acids for protein synthesis.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The mitochondrial DNA of trypanosomes exhibit an interesting exception to the central dogma: their pre-mRNAs do not have the correct information to specify a functional protein. Usually, this is because the mRNA is missing several U nucleotides. The cell performs an additional RNA processing step called RNA editing to remedy this.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: RNA editing is not just a phenomenon of trypanosomes. In the mitochondria of some plants, almost all pre-mRNAs are edited.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: RNA editing has also been identified in mammals such as rats, rabbits, and even humans.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The 3' ends of guide RNAs have a long poly-U tail, and these U bases are inserted in regions of the pre-mRNA transcript at which the guide RNAs are looped.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: This process is entirely mediated by RNA molecules. That is, guide RNAs—rather than proteins—serve as the catalysts in RNA editing.
